tenures.note: The federation's own Ladies Tag Team Champions through January and February 1992, undefeated at 10-0 until the Valkyries beat them on 19 February. The same two women — Katrina and Katherine — are named on the newsdesk's own tape of the federation's own Grapplemania, brawling with the Valkyries. This row was minted from the Summit's own broadcasts as the EMWA's Women's Tag Team Champions; the WeWF's own newsdesk carries them holding this federation's belt in the same months, and the rows in both federations' own standings are the same pair under the same name. Three of the newly served WeWF newsdesk editions — 30 January, 15 February and 25 February 1992 — reprint the UeWF's OWN published weekly rankings in full, singles, tag and ladies, and this entity stands in them under its own name. caption: Jake and Ric Shield of Russell, Ontario, who teamed with Johann Svenson at the second Summit against the men who had jumped two of their friends, and spent the following summer as the PWA’s top-ranked tag team without ever taking its belts — beaten twice by Da Boyz and once by the Dogs of War.

identity.note: Shares a team name with other registry "Shield"-named entities and the real-world WWE stable The Shield; nothing beyond the bare label is shared with either — filed distinct under the no-auto-merge rule.

notes: Receipt: the Summit of E-Wrestling’s own third night of 29 December 1991 announces the pair together — “hailing from Russell, Ontario, Canada, weighing in at 244 pounds, Jake “Canadian” Shield! And also from Russell, weighing in at 278 pounds, Ric “Tower” Shield!” — and the PWA’s own 1992 record announces the Shield Brothers “hailing from Russell, Ontario, Canada” and puts them in the ring against Da Boyz and their manager Da Boss, the same team under the same manager the Summit’s own card had staged eleven months earlier. Same hometown, same brother pair, same team name, same opponents. The PWA tenure above is folded in from that row; data/aliases.json redirects the retired id to this one. The retired row’s own with-less “distinct” guard against the real-world WWE stable The Shield is carried over unchanged. A third receipt, carried back from the pwa-1992 reciprocal guard main filed the same day and now superseded by this merge: the UFWS’s own Report #13 of 6 August 1991 has Jake Shield say “I will be leaving the UFWS soon, to start training my younger brother for the ring.” Five months later the Summit of E-Wrestling’s own third night announces the two of them together out of Russell, Ontario; eleven months after that the PWA announces the same team out of the same town. The 1991 guard called the younger brother an inference; the hometown the two feds announce is not one.
